raw_response:
I will keep it close to what I did before, because on 4.1 mu I cannot afford to gamble. I have grown peanut many years, and around here if the stand comes up even and the field stays clean early, half the crop is already settled. I do not put too much nitrogen on peanut, because if I push too much leaf, the pods do not fill well, but I will not cut fertilizer too hard either, because losing yield is worse than wasting some money. I will use an improved peanut seed this year, the kind people nearby have been using with steady results, not something strange. I will till the land with rotary tillage because my area is small and that is easier to manage. For fertilizer, I will aim a bit heavier on phosphorus and potassium than nitrogen. With well water in hand, I will plan a few irrigations if the weather turns dry, especially around flowering and pod setting. For pests and disease, I will spray a few times, not every few days, but I will not wait until the field is already damaged. If the season is normal, I will count on a decent peanut yield and keep the whole plan simple enough for two people to handle.
